description: Experience the exhilarating flavors of a classic Chinese Hot and Sour Soup, a culinary masterpiece that perfectly balances fiery spice with a delightful tang. This comforting bowl features tender pork, silky tofu, and various mushrooms, all swimming in a rich, savory broth. It is a truly invigorating dish that will warm you from the inside out.

ingredients.notes: mixed with 1/4 cup water for slurry

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rehydrate dried shiitake mushrooms if using, then slice them along with wood ear mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and tofu into thin strips. Shred the pork loin thinly. Ensure all ingredients are ready before cooking.

instructions.title: Marinate Pork
instructions.text: In a small bowl, marinate the shredded pork with 1 teaspoon of soy sauce and a pinch of white pepper for 10 minutes. This step helps to tenderize the pork and infuse it with initial flavor.

instructions.title: Simmer Broth and Main Ingredients
instructions.text: In a large pot or wok, bring the chicken or vegetable broth to a boil. Add the marinated pork, rehydrated shiitake mushrooms, wood ear mushrooms, and bamboo shoots. Reduce heat and simmer gently for 10 minutes to cook the pork and allow flavors to develop.

instructions.title: Add Flavorings and Tofu
instructions.text: Stir in the remaining soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rice vinegar, and white pepper. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed to achieve your desired balance of hot and sour. Add the tofu strips and simmer for another 5 minutes, allowing the tofu to absorb the rich broth.

instructions.title: Thicken and Swirl Egg
instructions.text: Give the cornstarch slurry a quick stir, then slowly pour it into the simmering soup while continuously stirring until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. Once thickened, slowly drizzle the beaten egg into the swirling soup, creating delicate, silky egg ribbons.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Turn off the heat. Stir in the sesame oil for a fragrant finish. Ladle the hot soup into individual serving bowls, garnish generously with fresh chopped green onions, and add a drizzle of chili oil if desired for an extra kick of spice. Serve immediately and enjoy the authentic taste of homemade Hot and Sour Soup.

tips: For an extra layer of umami, rehydrate dried shiitake mushrooms in warm water and use the mushroom soaking liquid as part of your broth.
Adjust the amount of rice vinegar and white pepper to your personal preference; these are the core 'sour' and 'hot' elements of the soup. Do not be afraid to taste and adjust.
Hot and Sour Soup is best enjoyed fresh, but leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop.
article:
Unleash a symphony of flavors in your kitchen with one of Chinese cuisine's most iconic and beloved dishes: Hot and Sour Soup. This culinary masterpiece perfectly balances invigorating heat with a tantalizing tang, all wrapped in a savory, umami-rich broth. Far more than just an appetizer, Hot and Sour Soup is a comforting bowl that awakens the senses and satisfies the soul, making it a staple in Chinese restaurants worldwide and a cherished dish in countless homes. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a curious beginner, mastering this classic will elevate your home cooking and bring the vibrant tastes of China directly to your table. Get ready to dive into the art of creating this deeply satisfying and incredibly flavorful soup.

## What is Hot and Sour Soup?
Hot and Sour Soup is a traditional Chinese soup renowned for its distinctive, complex flavor profile that lives up to its name. The "hot" typically comes from a generous dose of white pepper, often complemented by chili oil or other chili products, providing a warming, pungent heat rather than an aggressive burn. The "sour" element is primarily derived from vinegar, most commonly rice vinegar or, for a deeper, more authentic flavor, Chinese black vinegar. Beyond these two defining characteristics, the soup boasts a savory depth from ingredients like soy sauce, sesame oil, and various mushrooms (such as shiitake and wood ear), along with the earthy crunch of bamboo shoots. Shredded pork and silken tofu are common protein additions, and the soup is famously thickened with a cornstarch slurry, giving it a velvety texture, and finished with delicate ribbons of whisked egg. Originating from regions like Sichuan and Hunan, it’s now a universally popular dish that beautifully showcases the dynamic interplay of flavors inherent in Chinese cooking.

## Ingredients You'll Need
Crafting a delicious Hot and Sour Soup starts with selecting the right ingredients. Here’s a comprehensive list to guide your shopping:

*   **Broth:** 6 cups chicken or vegetable broth (low sodium preferred)
*   **Protein:** 8 oz lean pork loin or tenderloin, thinly shredded (or extra firm tofu, pressed and cubed for a vegetarian option)
*   **Mushrooms:** 4-5 dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and thinly sliced; 1 cup fresh wood ear mushrooms (or dried, rehydrated), thinly sliced
*   **Bamboo Shoots:** 1 (8 oz) can bamboo shoots, drained and thinly sliced
*   **Tofu:** 4 oz firm or silken tofu, cut into small matchsticks
*   **Flavor Base:**
    *   1/4 cup rice vinegar (or Chinese black vinegar for deeper flavor)
    *   3-4 tablespoons soy sauce (light)
    *   1 tablespoon dark soy sauce (for color, optional)
    *   1-2 tablespoons white pepper, to taste (don't be shy!)
    *   1 teaspoon sesame oil
    *   1-2 teaspoons chili oil or chili paste, to taste (optional, for extra heat)
*   **Thickener:** 3 tablespoons cornstarch mixed with 4 tablespoons cold water to form a slurry
*   **Egg:** 1 large egg, whisked
*   **Garnish:** 2-3 green onions (scallions), thinly sliced; fresh cilantro (optional)
*   **Optional:** 1-2 cloves garlic, minced; 1 teaspoon grated ginger

## Step-by-Step Instructions
Follow these steps to create your own authentic Hot and Sour Soup at home:

1.  **Prepare Ingredients:** Rehydrate dried shiitake mushrooms by soaking them in warm water for at least 30 minutes, then squeeze dry, remove stems, and thinly slice. If using dried wood ear mushrooms, rehydrate them similarly. Thinly slice the pork (or tofu). Mince garlic and ginger if using.
2.  **Sauté (Optional):** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat a tablespoon of oil over medium-high heat. If using pork, add the shredded pork and stir-fry until lightly browned, about 2-3 minutes. Remove pork and set aside. If using garlic and ginger, add them to the pot and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
3.  **Simmer Broth:** Pour the chicken or vegetable broth into the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Add the sliced shiitake mushrooms, wood ear mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and tofu. If you stir-fried the pork earlier, return it to the pot now.
4.  **Season the Soup:** Stir in the rice vinegar, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce (if using), and a generous amount of white pepper. Start with 1 tablespoon of white pepper and add more to your preference. Allow the soup to simmer gently for 5-7 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. Taste and adjust the sourness and saltiness as needed. This is where you can truly customize your Hot and Sour Soup.
5.  **Thicken the Soup:** Give your cornstarch slurry a quick re-stir. Slowly pour the slurry into the simmering soup in a thin stream, stirring continuously. Continue stirring until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. You might not need to use all of it.
6.  **Add Egg Ribbons:** Once the soup has thickened, slowly drizzle the whisked egg into the simmering soup while stirring gently with a fork or chopsticks. This creates beautiful, delicate egg ribbons. Stop stirring once the egg is cooked.
7.  **Finish and Serve:** Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the sesame oil and chili oil (if using). Ladle the Hot and Sour Soup into bowls. Garnish generously with sliced green onions and fresh cilantro, if desired. Serve immediately while hot.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results
Achieving restaurant-quality Hot and Sour Soup at home is easier than you think with these expert tips:

*   **Don't Skimp on White Pepper:** White pepper is crucial for the "hot" element. It provides a unique, pungent heat distinct from chili spice. Adjust to your preference, but a generous amount is key for authentic flavor.
*   **Balance the Sour:** Rice vinegar is good, but Chinese black vinegar offers a deeper, more complex sourness. Experiment with both. Add the vinegar towards the end of cooking to preserve its bright tang, adjusting to taste.
*   **Quality Broth Matters:** A good quality chicken or vegetable broth forms the foundation of your soup. If you have homemade broth, even better!
*   **Thin Slices are Key:** Ensure all your solid ingredients – pork, mushrooms, bamboo shoots, tofu – are thinly sliced or cut into matchsticks. This creates a harmonious texture in every spoonful.
*   **The Cornstarch Slurry:** Always mix cornstarch with cold water before adding it to hot soup to prevent lumps. Add it gradually, stirring constantly, until you reach your desired thickness.
*   **Egg Ribbons:** For fine, feathery egg ribbons, ensure your soup is at a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil, when you drizzle in the whisked egg. Pour slowly from a height while stirring gently.

## Serving Suggestions
Hot and Sour Soup is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in various ways:

*   **As an Appetizer:** It makes a fantastic starter for any Chinese meal, whetting the appetite with its vibrant flavors.
*   **Light Meal:** Paired with some spring rolls, potstickers, or a simple side of steamed rice, it can serve as a satisfying light lunch or dinner.
*   **Part of a Feast:** Integrate it into a larger Chinese banquet alongside dishes like Kung Pao Chicken, Mapo Tofu, or Egg Fried Rice for a truly authentic dining experience.
*   **Garnish Generously:** Always finish with fresh green onions. A sprinkle of fresh cilantro, an extra swirl of chili oil, or a dash more vinegar at the table allows diners to customize their bowl to perfection.

## Variations and Substitutions
The beauty of Hot and Sour Soup lies in its adaptability. Feel free to experiment with these variations:

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** Easily make this soup meat-free by using vegetable broth and omitting the pork. Boost the protein with extra firm tofu, tempeh, or a wider variety of mushrooms like enoki or oyster mushrooms. Ensure your chili oil and other sauces are vegan-friendly.
*   **Different Proteins:** Instead of pork, try thinly shredded chicken breast, shrimp, or even small pieces of fish for a different texture and flavor profile.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of white pepper and chili oil to suit your heat preference. For a milder soup, use less; for a spicier kick, add more!
*   **Vegetable Additions:** Feel free to incorporate other thinly sliced vegetables such as carrots, water chestnuts, snow peas, or baby bok choy for added nutrients and crunch.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Ensure all your soy sauces are gluten-free, and check labels on other ingredients like broth and chili paste.
*   **Authenticity Boost:** Seek out Chinese black vinegar (Chinkiang vinegar) for a more complex, aged sourness that many connoisseurs prefer over standard rice vinegar.

Whether you're craving comfort on a chilly evening or a vibrant starter for a celebratory meal, Hot and Sour Soup delivers every time. Its intricate balance of flavors and satisfying texture make it a timeless classic that’s a joy to prepare and even more delightful to consume. Dive in and discover the magic of this iconic Chinese soup!
